newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian mini-major Sibneft 1996 oil ouptut slips.
newsitem.headline: Russian mini-major Sibneft 1996 oil ouptut slips.

text.p: Russian oil mini-major Sibneft produced 18.61 million tonnes of oil in 1996, down from 20.34 million tonnes in 1995, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
Filipp Murashov also told Reuters that Sibneft -- whose production unit is Noyabrskneftegaz -- refined 15.62 million tonnes in 1996 compared with 16.53 million in 1995.
He gave the following details for 1996 output.
Sibneft produced 4.21 million tonnes of gasoline last year, 5.24 million tonnes of diesel and 0.79 million tonnes of jet fuel. No 1995 comparisons were available.
Vertically-integrated Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sibneft) is one of Russia's mini-majors.
It exported 23.5 percent of its 1996 crude oil output outside the Commonwealth of Independent States and 17.4 percent of its oil products to the same destinations.
He said the company, whose main production unit is Noyabrskneftegaz, planned to increase its presence on the oil and oil product sales market.
Sibneft was looking to acquire authorised capital in oil supply companies in the Urals and in western and eastern Siberia, he said.
Sibneft's authorised capital is 7.2 billion roubles, divided into 7,226,234 ordinary shares, each with a nominal value of 1,000 roubles.
ZAO Neftyanaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK) obtained 51 percent of Sibneft's shares at the end of 1996.
ZAO Rifail-Oil won 15 percent of Sibneft shares at an investment tender at the end of October, while unknown company Sins won a tender for 19 percent of the company's shares in September last year.
Rem Vyakhirev, chairman of Russian gas monopoly Gazprom, is board chairman of Sibneft.
